data.title: Card Deck Shuffle
data.statement:
Your task is to find the correct starting order of a deck of cards so that, when the cards are dealt according to the procedure below, they appear in the requested pattern.

<<The Challenge>>
Arrange the cards in a deck so that, when they are dealt using the following procedure, they produce the given target pattern.

Repeat the following steps until the deck is empty:

<<1.>> Deal the top card.
<<2.>> Move the new top card to the bottom of the deck.

<<Card Notation>>

The following mapping is used for suits:
{{S}} = Spades
{{H}} = Hearts
{{D}} = Diamonds
{{C}} = Clubs

The following mapping is used for card values:
{{1}} = Ace
{{7}} = 7
{{8}} = 8
{{9}} = 9
{{0}} = 10
{{J}} = Jack
{{Q}} = Queen
{{K}} = King

Each card is represented by a two-character string.

For example:
{{S1}} = Ace of Spades

The cover image of this puzzle shows one valid solution.

<<Example>>

Consider the following starting deck, where the leftmost card represents the top of the deck:

{{C7}}{{H9}}{{D8}}{{S0}}

The following shows how the deck changes at each iteration:

<<Iteration 1>>
Dealt order so far: {{C7}}
Remaining deck: {{D8}}{{S0}}{{H9}}

<<Iteration 2>>
Dealt order so far: {{C7}}{{D8}}
Remaining deck: {{H9}}{{S0}}

<<Iteration 3>>
Dealt order so far: {{C7}}{{D8}}{{H9}}
Remaining deck: {{S0}}

<<Iteration 4>>
Dealt order so far: {{C7}}{{D8}}{{H9}}{{S0}}
Remaining deck: empty

lastVersion.statementHTML:
Goal

Your task is to find the correct starting order of a deck of cards so that, when the cards are dealt according to the procedure below, they appear in the requested pattern.

The Challenge
Arrange the cards in a deck so that, when they are dealt using the following procedure, they produce the given target pattern.

Repeat the following steps until the deck is empty:

1. Deal the top card.
2. Move the new top card to the bottom of the deck.

Card Notation

The following mapping is used for suits:
S = Spades
H = Hearts
D = Diamonds
C = Clubs

The following mapping is used for card values:
1 = Ace
7 = 7
8 = 8
9 = 9
0 = 10
J = Jack
Q = Queen
K = King

Each card is represented by a two-character string.

For example:
S1 = Ace of Spades

The cover image of this puzzle shows one valid solution.

Example

Consider the following starting deck, where the leftmost card represents the top of the deck:

C7H9D8S0

The following shows how the deck changes at each iteration:

Iteration 1
Dealt order so far: C7
Remaining deck: D8S0H9

Iteration 2
Dealt order so far: C7D8
Remaining deck: H9S0

Iteration 3
Dealt order so far: C7D8H9
Remaining deck: S0

Iteration 4
Dealt order so far: C7D8H9S0
Remaining deck: empty
Input
Line 1: N — An integer, the number of cards in the deck.

Line 2: D — A string, the desired dealing order of the N cards after applying the dealing procedure.
Output
Line 1: A string — the initial order of the deck of N cards, so that, when dealt according to the procedure, they produce the desired final order.
Constraints
1 ≤ N ≤ 200

This puzzle uses a non-standard deck: cards may be repeated, and only the specified ranks are used.
Example
Input
4
C7 D8 H9 S0
Output
C7 H9 D8 S0
